summary:
SESSION 3 (this one) closes T15-F-002 / T15-Q-002 under the orchestrator's ruling, which also corrected its own earlier premise: `TestAckRefusesAReadThroughAboveAnyPositionTheRelayIssued` does NOT sign correctly today, and I verified that independently before touching anything. Exactly two edits, both in apps/relay/internal/api/handler/mailbox_read_mark_test.go, and nothing else in the tree changed. (1) A SECOND helper, `ackWithReadThroughSignedV2`, was ADDED beside `ackWithReadThrough`. It signs `CreateMailboxAckMessageV2(mailbox_id, device_id, envelope_ids, read_through)` - the transcript the handler actually builds whenever `read_through` is present (mailbox_handler.go:706-709) - and its comment names it the legitimate-client helper and names `ackWithReadThrough` as its attack counterpart. `ackWithReadThrough` itself is byte-identical: it must keep signing V1 because `TestAckSignatureMustBindReadThrough` depends on that being an attack. (2) `TestAckRefusesAReadThroughAboveAnyPositionTheRelayIssued` now posts through the new helper. NO assertion in it changed - every expectation and every message is byte-identical; the only additions are the call-site swap and a comment above the test saying why the legitimate helper is the right one there. The test now exercises what its own comment always claimed: a legitimate, correctly signed but buggy client presenting a position beyond the end of its own mailbox, refused 400 INVALID_SCHEMA. Under the T16 split (range bound behind VerifyMessageSignature) it stays green for the right reason instead of green by accident of ordering. I measured the ruling's three other claims rather than assuming them, with a throwaway probe test that was deleted afterwards (tree verified clean). All three hold: site 113 (`TestAckSignatureMustBindReadThrough`, in-range V1-signed) answers 403 INVALID_SIGNATURE TODAY, so it already reaches the signature check and the split moves nothing for it; its assertions are only 'not 200', 'bounded 4xx' and 'nothing deleted', all satisfied by 403. Site 153 (five malformed shapes) all answer 400 INVALID_SCHEMA from `decodeReadThroughShape` at mailbox_handler.go:681, which the split leaves ahead of authorisation. Site 203 (`read_through` nil) answers 200 and deletes, because the handler builds V1 there. A control probe confirmed the new helper's signature genuinely verifies: V2-signed IN-range returns 200 and really deletes, so the target test's 400 is the range bound and not a masked 403. `mailbox_ack_read_position_oracle_test.go` was NOT touched, as ruled - digest unchanged. SESSIONS 1-2 (unchanged on disk, digests re-verified this session): three new test files (rewalk-crash-safety.test.ts, relayClient.loopbackHostname.test.ts, mailbox_ack_read_position_oracle_test.go), flood-closure RED-6 re-parameterised 6 -> 60, and RED-4's cursorless assertion re-stated under the recorded ruling into a strictly stronger no-skip pair plus the new RED-4b. FULL RE-RUN on Node v26.5.0 (default non-login interpreter; a login shell starts v22.12.0, which lacks node:sqlite). `pnpm test` exit 1: 50 files / 293 tests, 7 failed, 286 passed - all 7 are session-1 REDs (4 loopback + 3 re-walk crash safety), none is mine and no pre-existing test changed colour. Go, all four configurations - untagged, -tags relayv2, -race, -race -tags relayv2 - each exit 1 with EXACTLY ONE failure, the ack-oracle RED `TestAckDoesNotAnswerTheMailboxEnvelopeCountToAnUnverifiedCaller`, 7 packages ok in each, and 0 DATA RACE in all four. `go vet ./...` exit 0. `pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e` exit 0, 3/3 (34.7 s). `pnpm typecheck` exit 0. Handover baseline for the implementer is therefore: 7 vitest REDs + 1 Go RED, and the target test is now green for the right reason. STATUS stays DONE_WITH_CONCERNS for exactly one reason, and it is not T15-F-002 (now closed): T15-F-003, the deliberately accepted coverage bound on the re-walk suite - one interruption point, one ciphertext regime - which the verifier should sweep and AC8 should carry as a residual. --- EARLIER CONTINUATION RECORD (session 2) ---
CONTINUATION of T15 after the orchestrator ruled on the two items the first session escalated. The first session's work stands unchanged on disk (three new files, RED-6 re-parameterised); this session did exactly two things. ITEM 1 (T15-F-001, authorised): flood-closure RED-4's single cursorless assertion `expect(counters.cursored[secondProcessStart]).toBe(false)` was re-stated, and nothing else in RED-4 was touched - the forward-progress, exit-0, history-1 and page-count assertions are byte-identical. It is replaced by TWO strictly stronger assertions plus a precondition: (a) if the resuming poll presents a position at all, that token must be one the RELAY ISSUED to the killed process for a page it actually received - tokens compared for EQUALITY only, never parsed or ordered - with `null` (cursorless) and `"0"` (the head, which skips nothing) admitted; (b) the same no-skip property in ENVELOPES, so it also binds the cursorless path: the resumed walk's first page may not start beyond `lastOffered + 1`, where lastOffered is the highest poison index the relay ever served the killed process. A precondition asserts the relay issued that process at least two continuation tokens, so (a) can never pass vacuously against an empty set. The three-part reasoning the orchestrator gave - green only because of the defect; relay-held floor rejected on the merits because `contact import` is an offline trust operation and the relay is adversary-adjacent; the replacement must pin the property and not the mechanism - is recorded verbatim in the file above the assertion, because re-stating an existing assertion must never happen quietly. The narrow half is NOT lost: a new case RED-4b pins that a poll with NO re-walk pending still presents no cursor (F-012 / T6-F-005), after first proving from the relay's own `next_cursor` that the import re-walk had run to the END of the mailbox. RED-4b is also the cursor-shaped T6-F-004 guard: a fix that never clears the re-walk presents a position there and turns it red. The counting proxy gained two recorded fields (`pollCursors`, `pollNextCursors`); `cursored` is untouched and still populated. Both rows pass on the current tree: RED-4 11.4 s, RED-4b 3.0 s. ITEM 2 (T15-F-002 check): all eight `read_through` values in the ack oracle ladder - 0, 1, 5, 6, 7, 39, 1000, 4096 - are WELL-FORMED cursor tokens by the relay's own shape rule, so NOTHING was changed in the Go test. The rule is `DecodeMailboxCursor` (mailbox_repo.go:322-339) reached through `decodeReadThroughShape` (mailbox_handler.go:422-438): non-empty, at most 15 characters, every character an ASCII digit, parseable as uint64. Each of the eight is a 1-to-4-digit decimal. Measured confirmation that the shape gate really passes them: today 0, 1, 5 and 6 answer 403 INVALID_SIGNATURE, which is reachable only PAST the shape check, and 7, 39, 1000 and 4096 answer 400 INVALID_SCHEMA from the RANGE bound at mailbox_handler.go:699. The ladder is therefore satisfiable under the T14-style split and the RED test needs no edit. CONCERN, and the reason this is not plain DONE: the ruling's premise that `TestAckRefusesAReadThroughAboveAnyPositionTheRelayIssued` stays green under the split 'because it signs correctly' is not correct on this tree. That test posts through `ackWithReadThrough`, which signs the V1 transcript `CreateMailboxAckMessage(mailbox, device, envelope_ids)` (mailbox_read_mark_test.go:84) while the handler builds the V2 transcript whenever `read_through` is present (mailbox_handler.go:706-709), so its signature does NOT verify. It is green today only because the range bound runs BEFORE `VerifyMessageSignature`; move the bound after it and that test gets 403 INVALID_SIGNATURE where it demands 400 INVALID_SCHEMA. I did not touch it - re-stating a second existing assertion was not authorised - so the orchestrator must decide before T16 starts. Full suite re-run on Node v26.5.0: `pnpm test` 50 files / 293 tests, 7 failed, ALL SEVEN pre-existing REDs from the first session (4 loopback + 3 re-walk crash safety); apps/cli 36 files / 228 tests (227 + RED-4b), 221 passed. `pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e` 3/3. Go: `vet` exit 0; untagged, -tags=relayv2, -race and -race -tags=relayv2 each show exactly one failure, TestAckDoesNotAnswerTheMailboxEnvelopeCountToAnUnverifiedCaller (the first session's RED), every other package ok, 0 DATA RACE. `pnpm typecheck` exit 0 across 7 projects. No pre-existing test changed colour.

findings.problem: The re-walk suite asserts crash safety at one interruption point (the third page of a five-page recovery walk) and at one flood depth (310 minimum-size poison, 7 pages). It does not sweep the interruption across every page of the walk, nor across the maximum-size ciphertext regime the RED-6 rows use.
findings.impact: A fix that persists the position only on some page boundaries - say, every fourth page - would pass this suite while still losing a message when the interruption falls in the wrong place. The property is 'the position is never in no durable place', and one sample cannot prove a universal.
findings.suggested_fix: Accepted deliberately, and unchanged by this continuation: the suite is ~31 s and a sweep over every page and both ciphertext regimes is minutes per arm. The verifier should sweep it - interrupt at pages 1 through 5 and repeat the SIGINT arm at ciphertext 262144 - rather than the RED suite paying for it on every run. Record it in AC8's residual list as a bound on what the tests prove, not as a defect.
